claim: Low-bit quantization-induced degradation (QiD) is greater for smaller models trained on proportionally more tokens (i.e., fully/over-trained small models), while larger models or those trained on fewer tokens experience negligible degradation, based on scaling laws derived from over 1500 quantized checkpoints (160M-12B parameters, 1B-206B training tokens).
stance_target: small, heavily-trained models (the class Qwen3-1.7B belongs to) are disproportionately vulnerable to low-bit quantization degradation, making quantization a live rival explanation
scope_conditions: 160M-12B parameter models, 1B-206B training tokens, 2-bit and 3-bit GPTQ quantization
quoted_support: We reveal that low-bit quantization favors undertrained large language models (LLMs) by observing that models with larger sizes or fewer training tokens experience less quantization-induced degradation (QiD) when applying low-bit quantization, whereas smaller models with extensive training tokens suffer significant QiD.

claim: For a 12-billion-parameter model, 3-bit quantization produces negligible degradation up to roughly 10^11 training tokens, after which degradation becomes pronounced; for much smaller models (160M, 1B parameters) this degradation onset occurs far earlier and is more severe, and the pattern intensifies further at 2-bit quantization.
stance_target: quantitative scaling relationship between model size, training-token count, and quantization degradation severity
quoted_support: 3-bit quantization results in negligible QiD for a 12 billion parameter LLM up to 10^11 training tokens, but beyond this point, QiD begins to become pronounced; For smaller models (e.g., 160 million and 1 billion parameters), QiD degradation occurs much earlier and is more severe. With even more extreme 2-bit quantization... the trend is similar, but QiD worsens sooner and more significantly.

claim: Projected low-bit quantization performance of future models trained on 100 trillion tokens (a milestone expected within a few years of the paper's 2024 publication) may not be desirable, particularly for smaller models, posing a forward-looking challenge for low-bit quantization research.
stance_target: the trend toward training smaller models on ever more tokens increases the risk that quantization is a genuine confound in small quantized-model studies
scope_conditions: extrapolated scaling-law projection to 7B/70B/405B models at 100 trillion training tokens
quoted_support: Our projection shows that the low-bit quantization performance of future models, which are expected to be trained with over 100 trillion tokens, may NOT be desirable. This poses a potential challenge for low-bit quantization in the future and highlights the need for awareness of a model's training level when evaluating low-bit quantization research.
